words.en: An area of land that is controlled by a particular country, ruler, or military force.

words.tr: phrase. 用电话交谈；在通话
words.ex: He is talking on the phone with his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他正在和妈妈打电话。
words.en: Using the telephone to communicate with someone.

words.ex: She plants flowers in her garden.
words.ex_cn: 她在花园里种花。
words.en: A garden is a piece of land next to a house, with flowers, vegetables, other plants, and often grass.

words.tr:
n. 暂停；停顿；
v. 暂停；停顿；
words.ex: There was a short pause before he answered.
words.ex_cn: 他回答之前停顿了一下。
words.en: To pause means to stop what you are doing for a short time before continuing.

words.ex: The dog wagged its tail happily.
words.ex_cn: 狗开心地摇着尾巴。
words.en: The tail of an animal, bird, or fish is the part extending beyond the end of its body.

words.ex: She added cinnamon spice to the cake.
words.ex_cn: 她往蛋糕里加了肉桂香料。
words.en: Spice refers to a substance used to flavor food, which is usually made from parts of plants, especially their seeds, fruits, or roots. It can also mean something that adds interest or excitement.

words.tr:
v. 注册；登记；
n. 登记簿；
words.ex: He will register for the course next week.
words.ex_cn: 他下周会注册这门课程。
words.en: If you register something, you officially record it or list it.

words.tr: n. 要洗的衣物；洗衣店；
words.ex: I put the dirty laundry in the washing machine.
words.ex_cn: 我把脏衣服放进洗衣机里。
words.en: Laundry refers to the clothes and linens that need to be washed or that have just been washed. It can also refer to the place or business where clothes and linens are washed and ironed.

words.ex: This small business is profitable.
words.ex_cn: 这家小企业有利可图的。
words.en: If something is profitable, it makes a profit or is beneficial.

words.tr: phrase. 站不住脚；失去平衡；卧床不起
words.ex: After the long walk, she sat down to get off her feet.
words.ex_cn: 走了很长一段路后，她坐下来休息双脚。
words.en: If something or someone knocks you off your feet, they surprise or impress you so much that you feel you have lost control of the situation.

words.tr: abbr. 盒式磁带录像机；“Video Cassette Recorder”的缩写
words.ex: We watched the movie on the VCR last night.
words.ex_cn: n. 昨晚我们用录像机看了那部电影。
words.en: A VCR is a machine that uses videotapes to record and play television programs.

words.ex: The ant moved its antenna to feel the ground.
words.ex_cn: 蚂蚁用它的触角感知地面。
words.en: An antenna is a device that sends and receives radio or television signals. In biology, it refers to the long, thin sensory appendages on the heads of insects and crustaceans.

words.tr: adj. 独自的；单独的；孤寂的；
words.ex: He lives in a solitary house far from the town.
words.ex_cn: 他住在离城镇很远的独自一人的房子里。
words.en: A solitary person or thing is the only one in a place.

words.ex: She put the cake in the oven.
words.ex_cn: 她把蛋糕放进烤箱里。
words.en: An oven is a device for cooking food, using dry heat.

words.ex: The number on the door is 5.
words.ex_cn: 门上的数字是5。
words.en: A number is a word or symbol that represents an amount or a quantity.

words.tr:
n. 委员会；佣金；
v. 委托；
words.ex: The commission met to discuss the new law.
words.ex_cn: 委员会开会讨论新法律。
words.en: A commission is a group of people who have been appointed to find out about something or to control something, or the act of doing this. It can also refer to a sum of money that is paid to someone for selling something, which is usually a percentage of the value of the goods sold.

words.ex: He needs surgery for his broken arm.
words.ex_cn: 他需要做手术来治疗断掉的胳膊。
words.en: Surgery is the medical specialty that uses operative manual and instrumental techniques on a patient to investigate or treat a pathological condition such as a disease or injury, to help improve bodily function or appearance, or to repair unwanted ruptured areas.

words.tr: phrase. v. （因病或受伤）卧床不起，不能起床
words.ex: After the accident, he was laid up for several weeks.
words.ex_cn: 事故后，他因伤卧床数周。
words.en: To be confined to bed or unable to work due to illness or injury.

words.tr: phrase. 因病卧床；因伤不能活动（通常指因疾病或受伤而需要卧床休息）
words.ex: He was laid up with a broken leg for several months.
words.ex_cn: 他因为断腿卧床了几个月。
words.en: To be confined to bed because of illness or injury.

words.ex: He wrote a check from his checkbook.
words.ex_cn: 他从支票簿里开了一张支票。
words.en: A checkbook is a book of checks which your bank gives you so that you can pay for things by check.

words.ex: He is the recipient of the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他是这个奖项的接受者。
words.en: A recipient is a person who receives something.

words.ex: He signed his name with a clear signature.
words.ex_cn: 他用清晰的签名签了名字。
words.en: A signature is a person's name written in a distinctive way as a form of identification in authorizing a document or letter.

words.tr:
v. 潦草地写；涂写
n. 潦草的笔迹
words.ex: He scrawled his name on the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他在纸上潦草地写了自己的名字。
words.en: If you scrawl something, you write it in a careless and untidy way.

words.tr: adj. 不值一读的；难以辨认的；难以理解的
words.ex: The handwriting was so unreadable that even the teacher couldn't decipher it.
words.ex_cn: 字迹如此难以辨认，以至于连老师都无法破解。
words.en: If something is unreadable, it is impossible to read because the letters or symbols cannot be recognized or understood.

words.tr:
n. 闪光；一刹那；
v. 闪光；闪现；
words.ex: The camera captured a sudden flash of light.
words.ex_cn: 相机捕捉到了一道突然的闪光。
words.en: A flash is a sudden bright light that quickly disappears. As a verb, it means to shine brightly for a short time or to appear or pass suddenly.

words.ex: The child looked sleepy after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 孩子晚饭后看起来想睡觉。
words.en: If you are sleepy, you are tired and ready to go to sleep.

words.ex: The firework went off at midnight.
words.ex_cn: 烟花在午夜爆炸了。
words.en: If a device or alarm goes off, it starts to ring loudly or make a loud noise. To leave a place, especially in order to do something. To happen in a particular way. To stop liking someone or something. To explode or fire. To decay or become rotten.

words.ex: He walks to class on campus every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上步行到校园上课。
words.en: The grounds and buildings of a university or college.

words.tr: phrase. 呈现；承担；接受；较量；雇用
words.ex: The sky takes on a pink color at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 日落时，天空呈现出粉红色。
words.en: To undertake or begin to deal with a task or responsibility; to hire someone; to acquire a particular appearance or quality.

words.ex: The hospital is a public institution.
words.ex_cn: 这家医院是一家公共机构。
words.en: An institution is a large important organization such as a university, church, or bank.

words.tr: phrase. v. 分支；分岔；从主干分出
words.ex: The road will branch off to the left after the bridge.
words.ex_cn: 过了桥后，这条路会向左分岔。
words.en: To divide into one or more subdivisions.

words.ex: The door opens on a metal hinge.
words.ex_cn: 这扇门装在一个金属枢纽上。
words.en: A hinge is a piece of metal, wood, or plastic that is used to join two things together so that one of them can swing or move freely.

words.ex: It's a myth that eating late at night causes weight gain.
words.ex_cn: 晚上吃东西会导致发胖，这是一种错误观念。
words.en: A myth is a traditional story, especially one concerning the early history of a people or explaining some natural or social phenomenon, and typically involving supernatural beings or events.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 利用…获利；从…中赚取利益
words.ex: He tried to cash in on the new trend.
words.ex_cn: 他试图利用这个新趋势赚钱。
words.en: To take advantage of an opportunity in order to make money or gain something.

words.tr: adj. 赚大钱的；获利多的；
words.ex: He took a lucrative job at a tech company.
words.ex_cn: 他去了一家科技公司做一份赚大钱的工作。
words.en: A lucrative activity or job is one that you can earn a lot of money from.

words.tr:
n. 负荷；载重；
v. 载入；
words.ex: The bridge can't hold such a heavy load.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥承受不了这么重的负荷。
words.en: A load is a large quantity of something that is carried by a vehicle, person, or animal, or the amount of work that a person or machine has to do.

words.ex: The company will advertise its new phone on TV.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司将在电视上为新手机登广告。
words.en: If you advertise something such as a product, an event, or a job, you tell people about it in newspapers, on television, or on posters in order to encourage them to buy the product, go to the event, or apply for the job.

words.tr: phrase. 可归结为；屈尊做某事
words.ex: It will come down to who works harder.
words.ex_cn: 这将取决于谁更努力。
words.en: If a problem, decision, or question comes down to a particular thing, that thing is the most important factor involved.

words.tr: phrase. v. 严厉斥责某人；痛骂某人
words.ex: The coach chewed him out for not following the game plan.
words.ex_cn: 教练因为他没有遵循比赛计划而严厉责骂了他。
words.en: To scold or reprimand someone severely.

words.ex: The mistake was trivial and didn't affect the result.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误不重要，没有影响结果。
words.en: If you describe something as trivial, you mean that it is not important or significant, or is not worth serious consideration.

words.ex: He burst into rage when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，他勃然大怒。
words.en: Rage is a feeling of intense anger that is difficult to control.

words.tr: v. 定居；安顿；解决；“settle”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 定居的；稳定的；
words.ex: They settled in Canada last year.
words.ex_cn: 他们去年在加拿大定居了。
words.en: If you feel settled, you have become used to your new home, job, or situation, and you feel comfortable and happy about it.

words.tr:
n. 抓痕；刮伤；
v. 抓搔；刮；
words.ex: The cat left a scratch on the door.
words.ex_cn: 猫在门上抓出了一道抓痕。
words.en: If you scratch something, you rub your fingernails or claws against it, often because it is itchy or irritating.

words.ex: He was put through a tough training program.
words.ex_cn: 他经受了一项严格的训练计划。
words.en: To cause someone to experience something, especially something difficult or unpleasant, or to connect a telephone call.

words.ex: He cooked dinner; meantime, the kids did their homework.
words.ex_cn: 他做晚饭；与此同时，孩子们在做作业。
words.en: The time between one event and another; meanwhile.

words.ex: He often criticizes his brother for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他经常批评他弟弟迟到。
words.en: If you criticize someone or something, you express your disapproval of them by saying what you think is wrong with them.

words.tr:
adj. 不锋利的；耿直的
v. 使变钝
words.ex: The knife is blunt and cannot cut paper.
words.ex_cn: 这把刀不锋利，切不动纸。
words.en: If you are blunt, you say exactly what you think without trying to be polite.

words.ex: The movie was fantastic!
words.ex_cn: 这部电影极好！
words.en: If you describe something as fantastic, you are emphasizing that you think it is very good or that you like it a lot.

words.tr: 短语. 就这一次；难得一次
words.ex: For once, she agreed with him.
words.ex_cn: 破天荒地，她同意了他的意见。
words.en: On one occasion; as an exception.

words.ex: The scientist created a clone of the sheep.
words.ex_cn: 科学家克隆了一只羊。
words.en: A clone is an organism or cell produced asexually from one ancestor or stock, to which they are genetically identical.

words.tr: adj. 卓越的；极好的；明亮的；灿烂的；
words.ex: He gave a brilliant answer to the math question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这道数学题给出了卓越的回答。
words.en: A brilliant person, idea, or performance is extremely clever or skilful.

words.ex: The injury led to a complication in his recovery.
words.ex_cn: 这次受伤使他的康复过程复杂化了。
words.en: A complication is a problem or difficulty that makes a situation harder to deal with.

words.ex: He has diabetes and must check his blood every day.
words.ex_cn: 他患有糖尿病，必须每天检查血糖。
words.en: A medical condition in which the body cannot produce enough insulin or cannot use insulin properly, leading to high levels of sugar in the blood.

words.ex: His eyesight is getting worse with age.
words.ex_cn: 他的视力随着年龄增长而变差。
words.en: Your eyesight is your ability to see.

words.tr: adj. 令人恐惧的；使人惊骇的；可怕的； v. “horrify”的现在分词；
words.ex: The accident scene was horrifying.
words.ex_cn: 事故现场令人恐惧。
words.en: If you describe something as horrifying, you mean that it is extremely unpleasant and causes great fear or shock.

words.ex: The loud noise at night will horrify the child.
words.ex_cn: 晚上的巨大噪音会吓到那个孩子。
words.en: To horrify someone means to shock or frighten them very much.

words.ex: She loves eating Korean food.
words.ex_cn: 她喜欢吃的韩国食物。
words.en: Korean refers to anything related to Korea, including its people, language, and culture.

words.tr: n. 单元格；细胞；牢房；小房间；
words.ex: Each cell in the spreadsheet holds a number.
words.ex_cn: 电子表格中的每个单元格都包含一个数字。
words.en: A cell is the smallest structural and functional unit of an organism, typically microscopic and consisting of cytoplasm and a nucleus enclosed in a membrane. It can also refer to a small room in which a prisoner is locked up or a device for producing electricity from chemical reactions.

words.ex: He obtained the position fraudulently.
words.ex_cn: 他通过欺骗手段获得了这个职位。
words.en: In a way that involves deceit, trickery, or intentional misrepresentation.

words.ex: The company made fraudulent claims about its product.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司对其产品做出了欺诈性的声明。
words.en: A fraudulent activity is deceitful or dishonest.

words.ex: The embryonic stage is the earliest phase of development.
words.ex_cn: 胚胎阶段是发育的最早时期。
words.en: In an early stage of development; rudimentary.

words.ex: The man was punished for fraud.
words.ex_cn: 这个人因欺骗而受到惩罚。
words.en: Fraud is the crime of gaining money or financial benefits by a trick or by lying.

words.tr: phrase. 集中（精力；注意力等）于
words.ex: He focuses on his homework every evening.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上专心做作业。
words.en: to direct your attention or effort towards something specific

words.ex: The reproductive system helps animals have babies.
words.ex_cn: 生殖系统帮助动物生育后代。
words.en: Relating to or effecting reproduction in living organisms.

words.tr: adv. 道德上地；伦理上地；
words.ex: He acted ethically when he returned the lost wallet.
words.ex_cn: 当他归还丢失的钱包时，他道德上地做了正确的事。
words.en: In a manner relating to moral principles or the branch of knowledge dealing with these.

words.ex: The company follows ethical practices in hiring.
words.ex_cn: 该公司在招聘中遵循伦理规范。
words.en: Relating to moral principles or the branch of knowledge dealing with these.

words.ex: From my standpoint, this plan is too risky.
words.ex_cn: 从我的立场来看，这个计划太冒险了。
words.en: A standpoint is a particular way of considering something, or a particular attitude towards it.

words.tr:
n. 问题；重要议题；发行（物）；
v. 发行；
words.ex: The main issue is lack of money.
words.ex_cn: 主要问题是缺乏资金。
words.en: An issue is an important subject or problem that people are talking about or arguing about.

words.tr: n. 流产；早产；误投；失败
words.ex: She had a miscarriage last month.
words.ex_cn: 她上个月流产了。
words.en: A miscarriage is the premature expulsion of a fetus from the womb before it is able to survive independently, or a failure to achieve the intended result of a plan or action.

words.ex: The doctor confirmed the stillbirth of their baby.
words.ex_cn: 医生确认了他们宝宝的死产。
words.en: The birth of a baby that has died in the womb.

words.ex: The fetal heart rate is monitored during pregnancy.
words.ex_cn: 怀孕期间会监测胎儿的心率。
words.en: relating to a fetus, especially in the womb

words.tr: n. 异常事物；反常现象；
words.ex: The strange weather this month is an anomaly.
words.ex_cn: 这个月奇怪的天气是一个异常现象。
words.en: Something that deviates from what is standard, normal, or expected.

words.ex: We need to buy pencils, paper, et cetera.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要买铅笔、纸等。
words.en: Used at the end of a list to indicate that further, similar items are included.

words.ex: The therapeutic massage helped her relax.
words.ex_cn: 这种治疗性的按摩帮助她放松了。
words.en: If something is therapeutic, it helps you to relax or to feel better about things, especially if you have been feeling worried or upset.

words.ex: The earthquake caused tremendous damage.
words.ex_cn: 地震造成了巨大的破坏。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as tremendous, you mean that they are very great in amount, extent, or intensity.

words.tr:
n. 潜力；
adj. 潜在的；
words.ex: The young athlete shows great potential.
words.ex_cn: 这位年轻运动员展现出巨大的潜力。
words.en: If you say that someone or something has potential, you mean that they have the necessary abilities or qualities to become successful or useful in the future.

words.ex: In some ways, he is better at math than his brother.
words.ex_cn: 在某些方面，他比他哥哥更擅长数学。
words.en: In certain aspects or to a certain extent.

words.ex: He makes the most of his time to study.
words.ex_cn: 他充分利用时间学习。
words.en: To use something to its fullest potential or to take full advantage of an opportunity.

words.ex: The scientist tried to replicate the experiment.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家试图复制这个实验。
words.en: To replicate something means to do or make something again in exactly the same way.

words.ex: He made a roadmap to learn English.
words.ex_cn: 他制定了一份学习英语的路线图。
words.en: A roadmap is a plan or strategy intended to achieve a particular goal.

words.ex: The new legislation bans plastic bags.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法规禁止使用塑料袋。
words.en: Legislation refers to the process of making or enacting laws by a government or other authority.

words.tr: phrase. 在适当的位置；适当
words.ex: The books are in place on the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 书整齐地放在书架上。
words.en: In the correct position or location; ready for use.

words.ex: He showed his disapproval by staying silent.
words.ex_cn: 他通过保持沉默表示反对。
words.en: Disapproval is the feeling that someone or something is bad, wrong, or unacceptable.

words.tr:
n. 结果；
v. 导致；
words.ex: The result of the test was good.
words.ex_cn: 这次测试的结果很好。
words.en: A consequence, outcome, or effect of an action or situation.

words.ex: He tried to dissuade her from quitting her job.
words.ex_cn: 他试图劝她不要辞掉工作。
words.en: If you dissuade someone from doing something, you persuade them not to do it.

words.tr: v. 制定法律；用立法规定
words.ex: The government will legislate new rules next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将制定新规则。
words.en: To legislate means to make or enact laws.

words.ex: The cellular structure of plants is very small.
words.ex_cn: 植物的细胞结构非常微小。
words.en: Relating to or consisting of cells; having a porous structure.

words.tr: n. 风暴性大火；大爆发
words.ex: The city was devastated by a firestorm.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市被一场风暴性大火摧毁了。
words.en: A firestorm is a very intense and destructive fire, often accompanied by strong winds. It can also refer to a situation where there is a lot of public anger and criticism about something.

words.ex: He will come forward to tell the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他将站出来说出真相。
words.en: If someone comes forward, they offer to do something or to give some information in response to a request for help.

words.ex: He asked for her consent before starting the project.
words.ex_cn: 他在开始这个项目之前征求了她的同意。
words.en: Consent is permission for something to happen or agreement to do something.

words.ex: He donate money to the poor children.
words.ex_cn: 他向贫困儿童捐赠钱。
words.en: To donate means to give something, especially money, to a person or organization that needs help.

words.ex: Follow the procedure step by step.
words.ex_cn: 一步一步地按照步骤进行。
words.en: A procedure is a way of doing something, especially the usual or correct way.

words.ex: You can eat no more than three cookies.
words.ex_cn: 你最多只能吃三块饼干。
words.en: used to emphasize that something is not more than a particular amount, number, or level

words.tr: n. 阿尔茨海默氏症；老年性痴呆
words.ex: She was diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease at the age of 65.
words.ex_cn: 她在65岁时被诊断出患有阿尔茨海默病。
words.en: A progressive disease that destroys memory and other important mental functions.

words.tr: n. 帕金森病（一种慢性神经退行性疾病）
words.ex: He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease at the age of 60.
words.ex_cn: 他在60岁时被诊断出患有帕金森病。
words.en: Parkinson's disease is a progressive nervous system disorder that affects movement.

words.tr:
v. 移栽；移植；
n. 移植；
words.ex: He will transplant the flowers to the garden tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天要把这些花移栽到花园里。
words.en: To transplant something means to move it from one place to another. In medicine, to transplant an organ, piece of skin, etc. means to use it to replace a damaged part in someone's body.

words.ex: He looks happy, but in reality, he is sad.
words.ex_cn: 他看起来很开心，但事实上，他很难过。
words.en: used to emphasize what is actually the case, as opposed to what people might think

words.tr: adj. 超越的；杰出的；卓越的
words.ex: The beauty of the sunset was transcendent.
words.ex_cn: 日落的美是超凡的。
words.en: If you describe something as transcendent, you mean that it is extremely good or impressive, often in a way that goes beyond the ordinary.

words.ex: He looks at the bug through a microscope.
words.ex_cn: 他通过显微镜观察这只虫子。
words.en: An instrument used for viewing objects that are too small to be seen by the naked eye, especially one that uses a combination of lenses to produce a magnified image.

words.ex: The blastocyst implants itself into the uterine wall.
words.ex_cn: 囊胚植入子宫壁。
words.en: A blastocyst is a structure formed in the early development of mammals. It possesses an inner cell mass which subsequently forms the embryo.

words.ex: He had a misconception that the earth is flat.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个错误认识，认为地球是平的。
words.en: A misconception is an idea that is not correct because it is based on a misunderstanding or a wrong belief.

words.ex: The embryo grows inside the mother's womb.
words.ex_cn: 胚胎在母亲的子宫内生长。
words.en: An embryo is an unborn animal or human being in the very early stages of development.

words.ex: He showed skepticism about the new claim.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个新说法持怀疑态度。
words.en: Skepticism is a questioning attitude or doubt towards one or more items of putative knowledge or belief.

words.ex: He did an analysis of the data.
words.ex_cn: 他对数据进行了分析。
words.en: Analysis is the process of considering something carefully or using statistical methods in order to understand it or explain it.

words.tr: phrase. 出于必要；由于必需
words.ex: They had to work on Sundays, by necessity.
words.ex_cn: 他们不得不在星期天工作，这是出于无法改变的条件。
words.en: If something happens by necessity, it happens because it must happen or because it is the only possible way that something can happen.

words.tr: adj. 全部时间的；专任的
words.ex: He works full-time at a grocery store.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家杂货店全职工作。
words.en: If you are a full-time worker, you work the normal number of hours or days in a week.

words.ex: The pope speaks to millions of people every year.
words.ex_cn: 教皇每年向数百万人讲话。
words.en: The Pope is the bishop of Rome and the leader of the worldwide Catholic Church.

words.ex: He defeated his opponent in the chess game.
words.ex_cn: 他在国际象棋比赛中击败了对手。
words.en: An opponent is someone who is competing against you in a contest, game, or argument, or someone who is opposed to an idea or plan.

words.ex: The public condemned the corrupt politician.
words.ex_cn: 公众谴责了这位腐败的政客。
words.en: If you condemn something, you say that it is very bad and unacceptable.

words.ex: In a sense, he is right.
words.ex_cn: 在某种意义上，他是对的。
words.en: You say in a sense to indicate that a statement is true in one way, but not in others.

words.tr: adj. 好争吵的；有争议的
words.ex: The plan is contentious because many people disagree.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划有争议，因为很多人不同意。
words.en: If you describe something as contentious, you mean that it is the subject of intense argument and disagreement.

words.tr: adv. 逻辑上；合乎逻辑地；
words.ex: He solved the problem logically.
words.ex_cn: 他逻辑上解决了这个问题。
words.en: In a way that is reasonable and based on good judgment.

words.tr: adj. 逻辑上的；合乎逻辑的；
words.ex: His argument is logical and easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点合乎逻辑，容易理解。
words.en: In accordance with the principles of logic; reasonable.

words.ex: The dentist placed a dental implant to replace the missing tooth.
words.ex_cn: 牙医植入了一个牙科植入物来替代缺失的牙齿。
words.en: To implant something means to put it firmly into something else, especially into a person's body.

words.ex: The fetus is growing inside the mother's womb.
words.ex_cn: 胎儿正在母亲的子宫内成长。
words.en: An unborn or unhatched offspring of a mammal, in particular an unborn human more than eight weeks after conception.

words.tr: phrase. 改变主意；重新考虑（某决定）
words.ex: After seeing the price, I began to have second thoughts about buying the car.
words.ex_cn: 在看到价格后，我开始对购买这辆车有了重新考虑。
words.en: To reconsider a decision or plan, often because one has doubts or concerns.

words.tr: phrase. + n. 广泛的禁止；全面的禁令
words.ex: The government imposed a sweeping prohibition on the sale of cigarettes in public places.
words.ex_cn: 政府对公共场所的香烟销售实施了全面禁止。
words.en: A sweeping prohibition refers to a comprehensive ban or restriction that applies broadly across a wide range of items, activities, or behaviors, often implemented by authorities to address societal, environmental, or health concerns.

words.tr:
v. 辩论；争论
n. 辩论；争论
words.ex: The students had a debate about homework.
words.ex_cn: 学生们就作业进行了一场辩论。
words.en: A debate is a discussion about a subject on which people have different views.

words.ex: A problem arose during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 会议中出现了一个问题。
words.en: If a situation or problem arises, it begins to exist or people start to become aware of it.

words.tr: phrase. 赞成与反对；正面与反面；利弊
words.ex: We listed the pros and cons before making a decision.
words.ex_cn: 我们在做决定之前列出了利弊。
words.en: The advantages and disadvantages of something, especially something that you are considering doing.

words.ex: The family is in a difficult plight after losing their home.
words.ex_cn: 这家人在失去家园后陷入了困境。
words.en: A plight is a difficult or adverse situation, especially one that is hard to escape. It can also refer to a solemn promise or pledge.

words.ex: The soil is too infertile to grow crops.
words.ex_cn: 这片土地太贫瘠了，无法种植庄稼。
words.en: Infertile land or soil is not able to produce good crops or plants. An infertile person, animal, or plant cannot have babies, eggs, or seeds.

words.ex: The flowers in the garden are artificial.
words.ex_cn: 花园里的花是人造的。
words.en: Made or produced by human beings rather than occurring naturally, especially as a copy of something natural.

words.ex: Artificial insemination has revolutionized livestock breeding.
words.ex_cn: 人工授精已经彻底改变了畜牧业。
words.en: The introduction of semen into the reproductive tract of a female, especially artificially, in order to achieve pregnancy.

words.tr: phrase. 体外受精；试管婴儿技术
words.ex: In vitro fertilization has helped many couples conceive a child.
words.ex_cn: 体外受精帮助了许多夫妇怀孕。
words.en: A method of assisted reproduction that involves combining an egg with sperm outside the body, in a laboratory dish.

words.tr: phrase. 订阅；同意；支持（某种观点或理论）
words.ex: He wants to subscribe to the news channel.
words.ex_cn: 他想订阅这个新闻频道。
words.en: to agree to receive and pay for a service or publication regularly, or to support an idea or theory

words.tr:
n. 亡命之徒；逃犯；被剥夺法律权益者
v. 宣布…为非法；使…成为非法
words.ex: The police caught the outlaw last night.
words.ex_cn: 警察昨晚抓住了那个不法之徒。
words.en: An outlaw is a person who has broken the law and who is hiding or running away to avoid punishment. To outlaw something means to make it illegal.

words.tr: phrase. 呼吁；有吸引力；使感兴趣
words.ex: The teacher appealed to the students to be quiet.
words.ex_cn: 老师呼吁学生们保持安静。
words.en: To make a serious or urgent request to the public for help or money; to attract or interest someone.

words.tr: phrase. 给予支持；提供帮助；声援
words.ex: The community came together to lend support to the local food bank.
words.ex_cn: 社区团结一致，支持当地的食品银行。
words.en: To lend support to someone or something means to help them by giving them your support or by doing something that helps them to be successful.

words.ex: He raised an objection to the new rule.
words.ex_cn: 他对新规定提出了反对。
words.en: An objection is an expression or feeling of disapproval or opposition; a reason for disagreeing.

words.tr: phrase. 代孕母亲身份；代孕母职
words.ex: Surrogate motherhood is a controversial practice in many countries.
words.ex_cn: 代孕母亲在许多国家是一个有争议的做法。
words.en: The practice by which a woman agrees to become pregnant and give birth to a child for another person or couple, typically because the other person or couple is unable to have children.

words.tr: phrase. v. 接受（现实、情况等）；与……达成协议；妥协
words.ex: He finally came to terms with his failure.
words.ex_cn: 他最终接受了失败。
words.en: To accept something that one cannot change, especially a difficult or unpleasant situation.

words.ex: He is tired, so he is bound to fall asleep soon.
words.ex_cn: 他很累，所以很快就会睡着。
words.en: Certain or destined to happen; inevitably going to occur.

words.ex: In essence, he is a kind person.
words.ex_cn: 本质上，他是一个善良的人。
words.en: You use in essence to emphasize that you are talking about the most important or central aspect of an idea, situation, or event.

words.ex: He felt the stigma of being unemployed.
words.ex_cn: 他感受到了失业的耻辱。
words.en: A stigma is a strong feeling of disapproval that most people in a society have about something, especially when this is unfair.

words.ex: He passed the test by virtue of his hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他凭借努力学习通过了考试。
words.en: Because of or as a result of something.

words.ex: The origin of this tradition is unknown.
words.ex_cn: 这个传统的起源不明。
words.en: The origin of something is the point or place where it begins, or the cause from which it arises.

words.ex: The school prohibits students from using phones in class.
words.ex_cn: 学校禁止学生在课堂上使用手机。
words.en: If a law or someone in authority prohibits something, they forbid it or make it illegal.

words.tr:
n. 坟墓；
adj. 严重的；
words.ex: They visited the grave of their grandfather.
words.ex_cn: 他们参观了祖父的坟墓。
words.en: A grave is a place where a dead person is buried. When used as an adjective, grave means serious or solemn.

words.tr:
n. 标签；
v. 用标签标明；
words.ex: The bottle has a label with the name of the drink.
words.ex_cn: 瓶子上有一个写着饮料名称的标签。
words.en: A label is a piece of paper, polymer, cloth, metal, or other material affixed to a container or article, on which is written or printed information or symbols about the product or item.

words.tr: phrase. 依靠；搁在；停留在；基于
words.ex: The bridge must rest on strong pillars.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥必须依靠坚固的支柱。
words.en: To depend or rely on something for support or as a basis.

words.ex: Exercise can reinforce your muscles.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以增强你的肌肉。
words.en: To reinforce something means to make it stronger or more effective.

words.ex: The boy defied his parents by staying out late.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩因为熬夜不回家而违抗了父母。
words.en: If you defy someone or something, you refuse to obey them or you do something that they do not allow.
